analysis: The code snippet contains calls to the `next()` method on two different iterators: `typeIt` (from `this.getParameterTypes().iterator()`) and `exceptionIt` (from `this.getExceptions().iterator()`). For `typeIt`, the `next()` is called inside a `while (typeIt.hasNext())` loop, so each call is guarded by a prior `hasNext()` check. For `exceptionIt`, the first `next()` is called only after an `if (exceptionIt.hasNext())` check, and subsequent calls are inside a `while (exceptionIt.hasNext())` loop, also guarded. The API method `next` is documented to throw `NoSuchElementException` if the iteration has no more elements. Because all calls to `next()` are preceded by a `hasNext()` check, the condition that would cause `NoSuchElementException` is avoided in every invocation.
